title: portolan manifest
description: Where the facts come from, what produces them, and what turns them into something to read. Generated by scripts/schema.mjs from the plugins this manifest declares; run `npm run schema` after changing them.

sources.description: Globs of the catalog fragments that make up the estate. They are merged, then validated as a union, so a fragment naming a peer it does not own is normal rather than broken.

plugins.description: How to run each plugin. A step names one by the name declared here.

plugin.description: A plugin declared above, one that belongs in this phase.

in.description: The directory to read, relative to the repository.

out.description: Where what comes back is written. A plugin names files; nothing it names is allowed to land outside this directory.

options.description: Passed to the plugin unread. What it accepts is described below.

extract.description: Steps that read source and write catalog fragments. They run first, before there is a catalog.

plugin.description: A plugin declared above, one that belongs in this phase.

in.description: The directory to read, relative to the repository.

out.description: Where what comes back is written. A plugin names files; nothing it names is allowed to land outside this directory.

options.description: Passed to the plugin unread. What it accepts is described below.

verify.description: Steps that read something observed - traces, a test's record - and answer with a fragment about the catalog somebody else declared.

plugin.description: A plugin declared above, one that belongs in this phase.

out.description: Where what comes back is written. A plugin names files; nothing it names is allowed to land outside this directory.

options.description: Passed to the plugin unread. What it accepts is described below.

generate.description: Steps that read the merged catalog and write something to read.

name.description: What the steps below call this plugin. It need not be the plugin's own name.

wasm.description: The default. The module gets no filesystem, no network and no environment, so a plugin from somebody else's repository can be run over your source tree without reading it.

url.description: https:// to download, or file:// for a path beside the manifest, as in file://plugins/gen-markdown.wasm.

sha256.description: Checksum of the module. Required for a download; optional for a local file, which it does not protect.

process.description: The escape hatch for a plugin that needs a toolchain. Same protocol, none of the sandbox, which is the trade being made.

cmd.description: The command to run, as in `go run ./plugins/extract-go`.

context.description: Slug of the bounded context this service belongs to. A Go module knows its import path, not which context owns it. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

contextName.description: What the context is called on the page. Defaults to the slug, titled.

contextSummary.description: A sentence or two on what the context is responsible for. Read on the context page and nowhere else.

classification.description: Whether the context is core to the business, supports it, or is generic and could be bought.

service.description: Slug of the service. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

serviceName.description: What the service is called on the page. Defaults to the title of its README, and failing that to the slug, titled.

repo.description: Where the source lives. Defaults to the module path in go.mod.

store.description: Slug of the database this service keeps its state in, the same one the sql extractor is given. It is here for the flows: a call on a repository lands somewhere, and only the manifest knows where.

peers.description: Which service answers for what this one calls, as the callee's package to its service id: a proto package for a gRPC client, the api id (the document's title and major version, `auth.v1`) for a generated HTTP client. The generated client names the package and the operation; only the manifest knows whose it is. A package with no line here is called as unknown and its steps stay unresolved.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory. One extractor writes one file, so that a fragment carries the provenance of the run that produced it.

context.description: Slug of the bounded context this service belongs to. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

contextName.description: What the context is called on the page. Defaults to the slug, titled.

contextSummary.description: A sentence or two on what the context is responsible for.

classification.description: Whether the context is core to the business, supports it, or is generic and could be bought.

service.description: Slug of the service. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

serviceName.description: What the service is called on the page. Defaults to the title of its README, and failing that to the slug, titled.

repo.description: Where the source lives. Defaults to the repository field of package.json.

store.description: Slug of the database this service keeps its state in, the same one the sql extractor is given. It is here for the flows: a call on a repository lands somewhere, and only the manifest knows where.

peers.description: Which service answers for what this one calls, as the callee's package to its service id: the api id for an HTTP peer, the proto package for a gRPC one. A package with no line here is called as unknown and its steps stay unresolved.

events.description: Which aggregate another service's events belong to, as the import specifier a policy reads them from to the aggregate id, so a policy reacting to a foreign event resolves.

source.description: The directory the layout starts in, relative to the input root.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.

context.description: Slug of the bounded context this service belongs to. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

contextName.description: What the context is called on the page. Defaults to the slug, titled.

contextSummary.description: A sentence or two on what the context is responsible for.

classification.description: Whether the context is core to the business, supports it, or is generic and could be bought.

service.description: Slug of the service. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

serviceName.description: What the service is called on the page. Defaults to the title of its README, and failing that to the slug, titled.

repo.description: Where the source lives. Defaults to the repository url in pyproject.toml.

store.description: Slug of the database this service keeps its state in. The models are read as its schema, and a call into the ORM lands on its lane; without it neither is claimed.

storeName.description: What the database is called on the page. Defaults to the service, titled, and the word database.

storeKind.description: Which database the models are the schema of. It picks the column types a field becomes; only postgres has a mapping, and a kind without one keeps the field's own name and says so.

apps.description: The Django applications to read, as import packages, for a project that keeps them somewhere a models module would not be found. Every package holding one is read when this is left out.

aggregates.description: Which model is the root of an application's aggregate, as the application to the model. Only needed where the application is not named after its root - `invoices` finds `Invoice` on its own.

peers.description: Which service answers for what this one calls, as the api id of the document vendored beside the client to the callee's service id. A client with no line here is called as unknown and its steps stay unresolved.

events.description: Which aggregate another service's events belong to, as the module a receiver imports the signal from to the aggregate id, so a policy reacting to a foreign event resolves.

source.description: The directory the applications are looked for in, relative to the input root.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.

storesOut.description: Name of the fragment holding the database the models describe, inside the step's output directory. Written only when store is set.

context.description: Slug of the bounded context that owns the service this document belongs to. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

service.description: Slug of the service the document describes. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

spec.description: The OpenAPI document, relative to the input root. Left out, the extractor looks for one.

api.description: Prefix for the ids of the rpc services this produces. Left out, it is built from the document's title and major version: auth 1.0.0 gives auth.v1, and a tag called users gives auth.v1.Users.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.

context.description: Slug of the bounded context that owns the service this document belongs to. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

service.description: Slug of the service the document describes. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

spec.description: The AsyncAPI document, relative to the input root. Left out, the extractor looks for one.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.

context.description: Slug of the bounded context that owns the service these migrations belong to. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

service.description: Slug of the service that owns the database. A store belongs to exactly one service. Defaults to the name of the input directory.

store.description: Slug of the database these migrations build. One service can keep state in more than one, and a slug is how the two are told apart. Give the go-domain extractor the same one.

name.description: What the database is called on the page.

kind.description: What kind of store it is.

repositories.description: Where the adapters live, relative to the input root: one package per aggregate, its migrations under migrations/ (every .sql that is not a .down.sql). The migrations are read from there, and so is which aggregate a table persists and which field a column carries - off the statements that write the rows, in Go, in TypeScript or in Rust.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.

title.description: Heading of the index page. The catalog does not name the estate, so this is the one thing the generator cannot derive.

traces.description: The recordings to read, as globs relative to the input root. OTLP JSON, one batch per file or one per line.

services.description: Which catalog service a resource's service.name belongs to, for an estate where the two differ. Without a line here a name is matched to the one service whose slug it is.

events.description: Which catalog event a wire name belongs to, for an estate where the event does not declare its wire name and the last segment of the event.name attribute is not the event's name in the model.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.

files.description: The flow files to read, as globs relative to the input root. Left out, every *.flow.md directly under the root.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory. Left out, flows.json.

modules.description: The modules to fetch, each pinned to a commit.

module.description: The module's registry-global name: registry, owner and name.

commit.description: The commit to fetch. A BSR commit is immutable, so a pinned fetch is byte-reproducible, which is what lets an offline run replay it from the tree. Left out, `ref` is resolved online and warned about, and refused offline.

ref.description: The label to resolve when there is no commit. Defaults to main.

paths.description: Directories of the module to keep, relative to its root; the rest is left behind. Left out, the whole module.

cache.description: Where the last run's files were written, repo-relative: the same path as the step's out. An offline run replays what is there and checks it against the lock beside it.

context.description: Slug of the bounded context the service belongs to. A .proto knows its package, not which context owns it.

service.description: Slug of the service that publishes or calls these protos.

paths.description: Directories of protos this service publishes, relative to the input root. They become what it provides. A directory fetch-bsr wrote carries its lock, and the lock says which module the protos came from.

vendored.description: Directories of client copies this service consumes, relative to the input root. They become what it calls. Listed rather than globbed: which copies a service may keep is a boundary a reviewer should see change.

peers.description: Which service answers for a vendored copy, as the proto package to its service id. A package with no line here is called as unknown and its steps stay unresolved.

modules.description: Which module a directory's protos belong to, as the directory relative to the input root to the module id. Only needed where there is no lock beside them to say.

defs.description: Whether a message imported from another file is promoted to a shared type, on the reasoning that the import is the author's own signal it is not local.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.
